narrative_purpose: Show a fossorial survivor as an accidental engineer of recovery: a burrowing animal mixing buried living soil up through the sterile ash cap and spreading fungal spores across the surface.
subject: A small stout burrowing rodent-like animal emerging from a tunnel it has dug up through a pale grey ash cap, pushing a mound of dark rich buried soil out onto the grey surface; fine pale fungal threads and tiny spores scatter from the upturned dark earth around the mound.
scene: A cutaway-into-surface view of grey ashland ground with the dark soil layer visible beneath, the fresh dark mound and burrow mouth the focal point on an otherwise sterile plain.
camera: Close low three-quarter shot on the burrow mouth and dark mound, surface-level.
light: Faint cyan life-glow on the fungal threads and the dark fertile soil; the surrounding grey ash stays dim and cool.
palette: Pale grey ash against dark fertile indigo-brown soil, living-teal spore glow, no warm accent.
style: Painterly naturalist plate, a small creature caught mid-act, observed.
detail_level: High detail on the animal, the dark mound and the drifting spores; plain softens behind.
composition: Burrow mouth and dark mound lower-centre, the animal emerging, scattered spores rising; leave open grey space to one side for later callouts.
consistency_notes: The teaching point is DARK buried soil being brought UP through the pale ash, plus spores spreading. Keep the dark mound and pale ash contrast clear. Cool Pandora palette, living-teal accents.
negative_prompt: no text, no lettering, no numbers, no labels, no arrows, no 3D-render or photographic look, no cartoon style, no neon glow
